title: Fake-DOM close-out: classify every census entry, file the prompt-section guards follow-up, report before/after
description:
This subtask holds the plan's "Report back" and "Out of scope, named" items. Review note 1b makes the final classification necessary, because about 24 single-element stubs the census catches are covered by no move piece. Those include `dashboard-routes`, `lin-4242-waiting-live`, the `lin-4114-*` suites, `lin-4241-settled-ruling-client`, `question-card-task-bound`, `task-page-*`, `close-out-client`, `common-*-filter-nav`, `run-limit-gating`, `runner-link-surfaces`, `lin-4024-*`, `lin-3254`, `lin-3136-settings-take-predicate`, `lin-2122`, `lin-2370`, `lin-3975-proposal-refresh`, `lin-4016-sessions-fold-parked` and `observation-waiting-block`.

* Put **every** remaining file in `HAND_WRITTEN_FAKE_DOM_FILES` in exactly one of three groups: moved, stopped (with the API that stopped it) or not attempted (with why). Give the census length before (the S1 baseline) and after.
* File one follow-up ticket for two things. First, removing the 7 `container.querySelector ? … : null` guards in `public/prompt-section.js`, listed by line at the HEAD of that time. Second, making the world helper the easiest thing to reach for in every new `lin-NNNN` witness (the cause the census treats as a symptom).
* Check that the `fake-dom.js` header's consumer list and "not modelled" lines are current, and that CLAUDE.md still names the census within budget.
* Post the final report on LIN-4255: families moved, families stopped and why, findings (fixed, filed or artefact), census before and after, and links to every PR's assertion map and test-name diff.

**Done when:** the report is on LIN-4255, the follow-up is filed, and the header and docs are current.

---

**Where the scope and design live.** Parent: LIN-4255. Read its description's **Implementation Plan** (the approved plan) and the Plan Review Verdict comment `98a20bc0-f43b-406c-bb64-8ce22860b08f`, which has notes for the builder. The parent's approved plan is where this piece starts. Follow it. Where the code shows the plan is wrong, change course and say so in a comment on LIN-4255.

* Session fit: fits one session
* Plan-review due: no. Covered by LIN-4255's approving plan-review (comment 98a20bc0-f43b-406c-bb64-8ce22860b08f, rev 1).
* Grounding commit: `b5391736` (LinearViewer origin/main; still HEAD when this breakdown was made on 2026-11-05).

**Rules for every move piece (from the plan):** test names and counts stay the same. Before and after, run `node --test --test-reporter=spec <file>` and paste the empty diff. Remove each moved file from `HAND_WRITTEN_FAKE_DOM_FILES` and from the `fake-dom.js` header's consumer list in the same PR. Delete both copies, the container and the `vm` sandbox. Never loosen an assertion that reads fake internals: map it to a real-DOM replacement and prove the replacement goes red under the mutation it guards. Every red is a finding, and the PR records it as fixed, filed or fake artefact. Serializer differences (`disabled=""`, escaping) are fixed in the test's regexes, never by relaxing the fake. Out of scope: the 7 `container.querySelector ? … : null` guards in `public/prompt-section.js`.

---

**Close-out stub (2026-11-05).** Implemented as approved: classification of the 25 remaining census entries (9 stopped with their API, 16 not attempted), comment-only census/header edits in PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2312](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2312>) (merged as `591bb959`), follow-up LIN-4292, and the final report on LIN-4255 (`4345cad0`, plus addendum `7998c5aa`). Problem statement, acceptance and scope above are kept as written; this description held no plan or research sections to prune. Full history is in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

parent.title: The shared fake DOM becomes the one in fact: move the hand-written client test fakes onto it, with a census (LIN-4252 tidy-after)

comments.body:
LIN-4267 (PR #2305, branch feat/lin-4267-prompt-section-p0-run-quota-runner-link-loadworld) — inputs for close-out classification:

1. Unreachable standard `__autopilot__` handler branch (public/prompt-section.js around lines 2090, 2118, 2532): no state draws that entry in any markup; only `__autopilot_stepper__` is drawn as an Autopilot entry. Possible dead code. LIN-4267 reports it and does not change it.
2. Shared `data-action="setup"`: the Go set-up control and the run-step set-up rung carry the same action, so a bare action selector matches Go first. Tests now name the rung. Not a product bug; a selector hazard.
3. The `__ai__` guard (LIN-4266 R8): no AI-off disabled-next-step press test was missing. The p0 witness presses the drawn disabled `opened-task-next-step` node through the real DOM, and is red when the guard at public/prompt-section.js:2515 is removed (mutation-proven, 1 red).

LIN-4272 beat 3 (close-out, repo changes): PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2312, head `8077c962`, branch `feat/lin-4272-fake-dom-close-out`, base `main` (1b83bbff, unchanged).

**Changes (comment-only; census membership and fake behaviour unchanged)**
- `tests/unit/fake-dom-census.test.js`: the nine stopped files name the API that stopped them, with file:line. The list doc comment says a stopped file keeps its entry. 25 entries, as before.
- `tests/unit/helpers/fake-dom.js`: `indeterminate` documented as a plain expando (no attribute to reflect). The consumer list was re-checked against the 37 importers and matches, so it is untouched. Spot-checked header claims against the fake: no defects.
- CLAUDE.md: not changed (110 lines / 11,802 bytes; budget test passes).

**Classification (25 remaining at 1b83bbff):** moved 0; stopped 9 (flight-companion-client; lin-3833-run-control and prompt-section-task-mode; lin-3136-settings-take-predicate; common-assignee-filter-nav and common-team-filter-nav; lin-4114-dismiss-order, lin-4114-inflight-lock and lin-4241-settled-ruling-client); not attempted 16 (single-element stubs, feasible). Moved since S1 (56): 31.

**Tests**
- Census + CLAUDE.md budget: 45/45 before and after; test names identical.
- Full unit suite: base 1b83bbff 23744/23744, branch 23744/23744; passing-name diff empty; 0 failures on both.

**CI** (`Tests` workflow on pull_request): Unit tests pass (9m33s), E2E shards 1-4 pass, Secret scan pass, CI success pass.

Not merged; merge is a separate step.

LIN-4272 beat 4 (follow-up filed): **LIN-4292**, Backlog, parent LIN-4255, related to LIN-4272, LIN-4254 and LIN-4289. The workspace API returns no URL for the issue, so the identifier is the reference.

Scope: removal of the 7 `container.querySelector ? ... : null` guards in `public/prompt-section.js` (line numbers at origin/main `1b83bbff`, verified by grep: 964, 995, 998, 999, 1008, 1120, 1137), and making `loadWorld` the default for new `lin-NNNN` witnesses. The ticket also lists the 10 `container.querySelector && ...` guards in the same file, which use the same pattern.

Why parent LIN-4255: LIN-4255's plan names these guards as its out-of-scope item, so the epic should track the follow-up.

Existing tickets checked before filing: LIN-4254 (moves, overlaps the witness-default part), LIN-4289 (`loadWorld` markup option, one piece of it). Neither covers the guards, so LIN-4292 is filed for both.

LIN-4272 beat 5: the final report is on the parent, LIN-4255, as comment 4345cad0-7840-4d8e-9344-735e343f660e. It covers the census (56 to 25), the 31 moved and 9 stopped families, the 16 not attempted, findings, and the course changes. PR #2312 is open with CI green on 8077c962; the follow-up is LIN-4292.

## Review — LIN-4272

Reviewed PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2312, head `8077c962`, base `main` `1b83bbff` (still origin/main HEAD). The PR changes only comments, in `tests/unit/fake-dom-census.test.js` and `tests/unit/helpers/fake-dom.js`.

CI: green on `8077c962` (Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan, CI success all SUCCESS; mergeable).

### What I checked
- **Staleness:** every commit since this ticket was created that touches the referenced files is a sibling move piece (#2297–#2311), and all of them are already in base `1b83bbff`. Nothing landed after the base.
- **Census counts:** the S1 baseline at `69e8f175` (#2297) has **56** entries, which I counted from the list in that commit. The PR head has **25**: 9 entries with a stop comment and 16 without. 56 − 25 = 31 moved, which matches the parent report's per-PR table. Each of the 25 entries is in exactly one group.
- **Stop citations, read at head:** I read the cited lines for all 9.
  - `common.js:2907`: `getBoundingClientRect` in `setupNavStickyHeight`, which `initNavBar` calls at `:2731`.
  - `flight-companion.js:653-665`: style write and offset/scroll read-back.
  - `proxy.js:51`: `scopeSelect?.value`. `render-proxy.js:51` renders it as a `<select>`.
  - `prompt-section.js:1565`: `el.value =` on run-harness. The test reads it at `:243`.
  - `question-cards.js:239-241`: bubbling `dispatchEvent`.
  - `prompt-section.js:2714-2715` → `common.js:1758-1763`: `readDispatchExecControls`.

  Every citation is accurate. The stub in each test confirms the API that stopped it: `getBoundingClientRect` stubs in both common-*-filter-nav suites, `dispatchEvent` recorders in lin-4114 ×2 and lin-4241, and a `value` stub in lin-3136. None of the 9 is relabelled as moved.
- **`fake-dom.js` header consumer list:** I compared the basenames in the header with every file that imports `fake-dom`, `client-world` or `live-console-world`, and they match. The only differences are that the census file names the fake without importing it, and that the header also mentions the `common.js` and `observation.js` scripts. The new `indeterminate` line is accurate. `dispatchEvent` is documented as inert, and the code agrees (`fake-dom.js:252` at head).
- **CLAUDE.md:** the fake-DOM census enforcement is still named at line 58. The file is 110 lines / 11,802 bytes. `claude-md-line-budget` passes.
- **Follow-up LIN-4292:** it is filed in Backlog under LIN-4255 and covers both parts the ticket asks for. I re-checked the 7 guard lines with `git show 1b83bbff:public/prompt-section.js | grep "querySelector ?"`: 964, 995, 998, 999, 1008, 1120 and 1137, which matches exactly.
- **Final report on LIN-4255 (`4345cad0`):** it has families moved (with PRs and where each PR body keeps its assertion map and name diff), families stopped with the API that stopped each, the not-attempted list, findings, and the census before/after.
- **Tests at head:** `node --test fake-dom-census + claude-md-line-budget` passed 45/45.
- **Mutation check:** I deleted the `lin-4114-inflight-lock` entry from the list, which made the census go red (1 fail, 42 pass), so the ratchet still holds stopped entries. Reverted afterwards.
- **Regression risk:** the change is comment-only and changes no runtime or test behaviour.
- **Isolated or a class:** isolated. This is close-out documentation, so there are no sibling instances to chase. The class of the guard pattern is already handed to LIN-4292, which includes the 10 `&&`-form guards in the same file.

### Findings
1. **Report points at an unreachable file (minor, inside: the ticket's "not attempted (with why)" and "post the final report" items).** Section 4 of `4345cad0` says "Full table: `lin-4272-beat2-classification.md` in the scratchpad". That is a local session file nobody else can open. For the 12 under "Others", the report also says only "feasible with the modelled APIs", which explains why a move is possible but not why none was attempted.
   - **Fix for close-out:** post a short addendum comment on LIN-4255. It should say that the scratchpad pointer is withdrawn, and that the 16 were not attempted because no LIN-4255 move piece had them in scope (LIN-4255 review note 1b; their moves sit with LIN-4254 / LIN-4292). It should then list the 16 inline with that reason, keeping the 4 pre-move checks as already written.
2. **Wrong beat number in the census doc comment (nit, fix optional).** The new doc comment says "(LIN-4272 classification, beat 2)", but the work was recorded as beat 3 on this ticket. The parent report also calls it beat 2, so this is consistent if beat 2 means the classification pass. Close-out can leave it.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside** (Done-when: "the header and docs are current"): the header and census comments are current only once PR #2312 is merged. Today they exist only on the branch.
  - **Before the merge:** close-out re-checks CI is green on `8077c962`, or on whatever head it merges, then merges #2312.
  - **Distinguishing check after merging:** `git show origin/main:tests/unit/fake-dom-census.test.js | grep -c "// stop:"` = 9, and the list length is still 25.
- **Inside** (the ticket's "Post the final report" and "not attempted (with why)" items): the report must stand without a local scratchpad file. CI cannot see Linear.
  - **Before the merge:** close-out posts the LIN-4255 addendum described in finding 1. It is discharged when that comment lists all 16 not-attempted files with a reason and has no scratchpad reference.
- **Inside** (the census stop classification): CI does not check that the file:line citations in the stop comments are correct, because they are comments.
  - **Discharged:** I checked all 9 citations against the source at `8077c962` (see above).

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger: merge #2312 on a green head, and post the LIN-4255 addendum that replaces the scratchpad pointer with the inline not-attempted reasons. The classification is complete and every claim I checked is accurate: 56 → 25, with 31 moved, 9 stopped and 16 not attempted. The follow-up is filed with verified line numbers, the header and CLAUDE.md are current, and CI is green.

## Close-out — LIN-4272

**Merged:** PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2312, squash-merged as `591bb9596159df600eeff47dd7205e7d41b31bb1`, pinned with `--match-head-commit 8077c962` (the commit CI passed on; base `1b83bbff` was still origin/main). Comment-only changes to `tests/unit/fake-dom-census.test.js` and `tests/unit/helpers/fake-dom.js`. No deploy impact (test files only), so there is no post-deploy step.

**Review verdict:** Approve with a ledger (comment `cc454f5b`).

**Changes I made after approval**
- No code commits. The one fix review asked for was a comment on LIN-4255: addendum `7998c5aa` withdraws the scratchpad pointer in report `4345cad0` section 4 and lists all 16 not-attempted files inline with the reason (no LIN-4255 move piece had them in scope, per plan-review note 1b; the moves sit with LIN-4254 / LIN-4292), keeping the 4 pre-move checks.
- Review finding 2 (the "beat 2" wording in the census comment) was marked optional and consistent with the parent report; left as is.
- LIN-4292 had no priority: set to Low (1), reason on the ticket. Its type label could not be set (the proxy PATCH has no label field); noted on the ticket that `Improvement` fits.

**Ledger**
- *Header and docs current only once merged (inside):* done. On `main` at `591bb959`, the census file has 9 `// stop:` comments and the list is 25 entries (`gh api` fetch of the file at `main`).
- *Final report must stand without a scratchpad file (inside):* done, addendum `7998c5aa` (16 = 4 + 12; 31 moved + 9 stopped + 16 not attempted = 56).
- *Stop citations (inside):* already discharged by review (all 9 read at head).
- No named monitor or rollback was required by the ledger.

**CI:** the `Tests` workflow was green on `8077c962` (Unit tests, E2E shards 1-4, Secret scan, CI success) before the merge. The post-merge `Tests` run on `591bb959` was still queued when I closed, so it is not seen green. The change is comment-only and review's test run (census + budget 45/45) passed on the head.

**Follow-ups:** LIN-4292 (already filed; guards + `loadWorld` default). Existing-ticket check was done at filing against LIN-4254 and LIN-4289. The unfiled items from the report (`data-action="setup"` hazard; `task-mode-routes.test.js` 15 ms sleep flake) are not inside this task's scope; the flake still needs a ticket from the owner of task-mode routes.

**Description:** pre-prune snapshot confirmed in `/issues/LIN-4272/snapshots` (captured 18:09:09Z, carries the original description). The description held no plan or research sections, so nothing was removed; I appended a short stub recording the PR, the plan as implemented, and where the history lives.

## Autopilot run summary (stepper) — LIN-4272

**Beats (one warm session, kind=implementation):** 1/5 ground + census snapshot (56 at S1 → 25) · 2/5 classify all 25 (0 moved, 9 stopped with file:line API, 16 not attempted) · 3/5 header/census comments + PR · 4/5 follow-up filed · 5/5 final report on LIN-4255.
Then review (conditional Approve, comment cc454f5b) and close-out.

**Evidence I checked myself:**
- PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2312: 2 files, comment-only; all 7 checks green on head 8077c962 before merge; squash-merged as 591bb959 (MERGED, LIN-4272 state Done).
- Follow-up LIN-4292 (Backlog, child of LIN-4255): the 7 `container.querySelector ? … : null` guards by line + making `loadWorld` the default for new lin-NNNN witnesses.
- LIN-4255 final report 4345cad0 + addendum 7998c5aa (16 not-attempted reasons inline).
- Findings: filed LIN-4286, 4287, 4289, 4290, 4292.

**What's left / not claimed:** the post-merge `Tests` run on main at 591bb959 was still in progress when I wrote this (change is comment-only). The `task-mode-routes` timing flake has no ticket (owner call). LIN-4292 needs its type label applied by hand (proxy can't set labels).

## Survey 1a (round 3)

**1. Why was this difficult?** The code was not hard. The difficulty was that the facts kept moving. By the time I started, 13 PRs had merged in four hours. The ticket's family list was already stale: observation-waiting-block had moved, and prompt-section-task-mode was a stop. Two of the plan's predictions had flipped (live-console moved; lin-4016 moved). The census list was the only canonical record, and it held file names, not reasons. The reasons lived in PR bodies whose section names all differed, plus ruling comments. So classifying 25 files was archaeology plus first-hand reading. The census detector sits inside a test file, so to ask "what shape triggered this file" I had to copy it out to a scratch file.

**2. What I would have done first.** Run the detector over the remaining list on day one, before any move. And give every move PR one shared evidence template (assertion map, name diff, stops), so a close-out links sections instead of hunting for them.

**3. What I would tidy.**
- Move `fakeDomShapes` into `tests/unit/helpers/`, so a tool can ask why a file is flagged.
- Turn the stop reasons I added as comments into data the census asserts. Today a comment can go stale silently.
- Fold LIN-4254 into LIN-4292 or close it. They overlap.

**4. If the area were how I'd want it.** Each move PR would update a classification next to the list as it went. The close-out would then be a short review of that record, not a ticket.

**5. What the ticket or plan got wrong.**
- The family list was stale on arrival.
- "About 24 stubs no move piece covers" was half right. Nine of the 25 were stops on unmodelled APIs (`<select>.value`, `getBoundingClientRect`, bubbling `dispatchEvent`). Four of those had no prior record (lin-3136, both common-*-filter-nav, and the lin-4114/4241 dispatch trio, which counts as one).
- "Seven guards" counted only the ternary spelling. Ten `container.querySelector && …` guards in the same file do the same job.
- It said to remove moved files from the header's consumer list. The accepted ruling said they join it.

**6. What it left behind.**
- Stop reasons now live in two places: census comments and the LIN-4255 report.
- LIN-4292 and LIN-4254 overlap.
- The four new stops were never fed back to the sibling pieces or the fake's header. They exist only in the list comments and my report.
- One `indeterminate` line in the header.
- Simpler: the fake's header is now complete, and the list says why each stopped file is still there.

**7. Did the larger scope pay?** I did not read the Survey, so I can't compare against its recommendation. Within my piece, classifying all 25 paid for itself: it found four stops nobody had recorded, and showed that 16 files are feasible to move with the fake as it stands. Where it cost more than it saved: verifying the fake header's accuracy duplicated checks the move PRs had already made, and the full-suite runs for a comment-only PR were ceremony. I would also have split LIN-4292. Guard removal (production code, a bounded diff) and making `loadWorld` the default for new witnesses (a convention plus a check) have different owners and sizes, and bundling them makes the ticket harder to close. My line: classify everything, record the stops as data, and file one ticket per concern.
